title: Most news feeds are built to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
body:
It is easy to assume that personalization just means showing you more of what you already clicked on. If you read one article about a new tech launch, the algorithm assumes you want ten more. But that is not true personalization. That is just a feedback loop that narrows your world.

At Headlinne, we look at it differently. We believe a recommendation engine should learn what you care about by understanding the substance of what you actually read. It is not about tracking every tap or dwell time. It is about identifying the topics, perspectives, and depth that you engage with over time.

When we build our AI, we focus on the reader's intent. Do you want quick updates on global markets? Are you digging deep into climate policy? Our engine learns these patterns without relying on shallow tricks. The goal is to save you time by filtering out the noise and delivering the stories that actually matter to your specific interests.

Good technology should respect your attention rather than exploit it. Personalization should be a tool that helps you stay smarter, not a trap that keeps you stuck in a cycle of irrelevant content.
cta: See how we are changing the way you stay informed at HEADLINNE.com.
